title: Conditional Expressions (Ternary Operator) 🎛️
description: Write compact if‑else logic in a single line for cleaner code.

slides.title: A Shortcut for Simple if‑else
slides.content:
# The Ternary Operator

Python's conditional expression syntax:
```
value_if_true if condition else value_if_false
```
Example:
```python
status = "Open" if port == 80 else "Closed"
```
It evaluates the condition and returns one of the two values.

slides.title: Ternary in Action
slides.content: Assign a message based on a check:
slides.codeSnippet:
port = 22
msg = "SSH" if port == 22 else "Unknown"
print(f"Service: {msg}")

quizData.question: What is the output of: `x = "Yes" if 10 > 5 else "No"`?
quizData.explanation: 10 > 5 is True, so the value before `if` is chosen.

slides.title: Where to Use Ternary
slides.content:
# Best for Simple Assignments or Returns

* Setting a variable based on a condition
* Building a string for logging
* Passing a value to a function

```python
print(f"Port {p} is {'open' if p in open_ports else 'closed'}")
```
Not suitable for complex logic with many statements – use full if for that.

slides.title: Nested Ternary (Careful!)
slides.content:
You can chain them, but readability suffers:
```python
level = "critical" if score>90 else "high" if score>70 else "low"
```
Better to use if‑elif‑else for multi‑way.

slides.title: Overuse Alert ⚠️
slides.content:
## Don't Sacrifice Clarity

```python
# Hard to read
x = (a*b if a>b else b*a) if condition else (a+b)
```
If you squint, break it out with normal if/else.

quizData.question: The ternary operator can contain multiple statements.
quizData.explanation: It evaluates to a single value; you cannot execute statements like `print()` inside it.

slides.title: Ternary vs Full if
slides.content:
# When to Use Which

| Situation | Use |
|-----------|-----|
| Choose between two values | Ternary |
| Execute a block of code | Full if |
| Need multiple elifs | Full if‑elif |
| Very short condition inline | Ternary |

Both have their place. Readability rules.

slides.title: Pro Tip 💡
slides.content:
## Use Ternary in f‑strings

Embed decisions directly in output:
```python
print(f"Result: {'OK' if code==200 else 'Fail'}")
```
Makes logging concise.
